I've got lyme disease myself, and I've done tonnes of research on the subject, and I'm here to tell you that this is wrong. The average is closer to 8 hours. Some people are lucky and they won't get it even after being a 48 hour meal. Some people are unlucky and get it with only a 1 hour feeding session. There are also fast feeding, soft body ticks that can transmit lyme in 15 minutes.

The way the tick is removed is also a big factor. If you squeeze their body, that will force some of the blood and saliva back into the wound, and that raises your chances of contracting lyme. The safest way to do it, is to take a pair of tweezers, grab the head of the tick or as close to it as you can get without digging into the bite, and pull upwards (as opposed to straight out, they usually bite at an angle).

Also, the bullseye rash does not show up on every patient, nor does it always look like a bullseye; it only shows up 36% of the time according to the most recent data. And only 17% of lyme patients recall a tick bite. You can see some examples of rashes here https://youtu.be/bULY7Dp1NDA?t=14m5sYouTube, and there are lots of good seminars here https://youtu.be/bULY7Dp1NDA?list=PLG6GrsCqslFfwwOGoIz1P2q9gfXrKXkM2YouTube

Lyme Disease consists of anywhere from 1 to 30 different pathogens, and we know of 100+ species of each of the most common two, Borrelia and Bartonella. It's a scary disease; it's expensive to treat, and there are a lot more ticks out this year than there have been in the past. So, be careful; stay away from tall grass, and use permethrin based insecticide on your clothing if you do plan on spending a lot of time outdoors in an area where you might encounter ticks; it'll stay on your clothes through a handful of wash cycles, and pull your socks over your jeans as well. You'll look silly, but you won't have ticks crawling up your leg inside your pants.

Lyme causing borrelia is associated with dementia, schizophrenia, extreme anxiety and depression, memory problems, sensory processing problems, ALS, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid disease; there are people that experience arrhythmia and heart failure as a result of this disease, and unless you catch it early, within a few weeks, it's going to take more than 4 - 6 weeks to treat it. A sizable chunk of patients that discover this disease a year or more after infection require 1-3 years worth of antibiotics, and that comes with it's own complications ranging from gall bladder removal, kidney and liver problems to destruction of your microbiome leading to things like C-difficile and chronic fatigue syndrome.

The long course of antibiotics is necessitated because lyme has a lot of characteristics that make it hard to eradicate. The spirochetes, the main pathogen, can curl up into what's called a cyst form, which shields them from antibiotics and hides their surface antigens. So your immune system has trouble fighting it. It also has a long division period, around 24 hours. The other common co-infections have similarly long division times too. They can also shift into what's called a cell wall deficient form or L-form, which renders antibiotics that act on the cell wall ineffective. They can also form biofilm colonies, where they're shielded from antibiotics, but they come and go from these colonies, and they're vulnerable as they do.

They can also take up residence within cells, including red blood cells, fibroblasts, and collagen, rendering antibiotics that don't penetrate the intracellular compartment useless. It also gives them a free ride into immunoprivileged areas like the central nervous system. While it's moving around, it also throws off BLP molecules which incite the immune system to attack whatever they land on. It can also rotate out surface antigens, and some of those surface antigens resemble myelin sheaths and connective tissue among other things, causing your immune system to attack anything resembling those antigens. Through this mechanism, it can cause autoimmune disorders. 30% of people with rheumatoid arthritis also have lyme. In the mid 2000's, 7 out of 10 dementia patients examined post-mortem in a New Jersey hospital were found to have Lyme borrelia in their brains via a PCR test with 99% specificity.

Anyways, it's a scary disease. It's a diagnostic nightmare (the western blot detects about 66% of patients with lyme. PCR's detect 30%. The ELISA detects 20-50% of cases depending on your location, and there are plenty of patients that are seronegative on all of these, yet they get better when they're treated for lyme after a clinical diagnosis.) So avoid this; be careful out there, and if you find a tick latched onto you, get it tested. If you get a rash, see your doctor, and ask for 30 days of doxycycline. It's a whole hell of a lot easier to kill if it's caught early, and people can and do die from this disease. There are other things like the powassan virus and tick paralysis (caused by a neurotoxin) that can result in death much more readily.

Daily Devotional

July 11

31 What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us?32 He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? - Romans 8:31-32 (KJV)

Paul had been teaching about all the power we, who are born again, have by having the Holy Spirit living in us, and since this is true, who could possibly ever be successful against us. Since we have the power of God living in us, when born again, we are given power over this world and heaven (Matthew 28:18), as well as the devil (James 4:7). If the born again Christian could just realize what power has been given to us, both in the physical and in the spiritual worlds, we would be able to live the victorious life that God intends us to have (John 10:10). Jesus accomplished it all for us and few of us ever even know that we have all this power living inside our spirits. We have the power of life and death in the words we speak (Proverbs 18:21), and we don’t use it properly.

God wants to give us, His children, all that we need, and when we pray and ask in accordance with His will, He always gives it to us (1 John 5:15). When we don’t receive what we pray for, it is because we ask amiss (James 4:3), as God is always faithful to provide for us. What a wonderful God we have, who sent His Son to die for us, just so that He could again have fellowship with us (John 17:3). What love that is, and it sure does illustrate that God is love (1 John 4:8). This same kind of love is now in those of us who have been born again, as it is part of the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23). We need to show this love to all our brothers and sisters in the Lord, as well as the rest of the world. Praise God for all He has done for us.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
